# Tanya's Sprint Retro

Tanya: "We shipped the async decision widget. Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter. The Zephyr integration was the key unlock."

segments.exact: We shipped the async decision widget.
Velocity was 23 points, highest this quarter.
The Zephyr integration was the key unlock.

observations.why: The Zephyr integration is spoken of AS an unlock — a thing (a mechanism) named as another thing (a key), performing metaphor rather than merely describing importance.

observations.why: Shipping a completed deliverable performs competence — mastery and craft brought to delivery.
Superlative framing of velocity positions achievement and standing as the appealed-to good.
Naming an integration as the decisive enabler of success frames capability and mastery as the motive.

observations.why: Confident causal attribution stated as flat assertion; no hedging pulls it to notion, no ratification or operational language lifts it to decision.

observations.why: Flat instrumental delivery with no performance markers establishes the document's baseline register.

mints.name: TechnicalUnlockNaming
mints.title: the key unlock
mints.frame: Is the speaker naming a mechanism as the causal unlock in native pipeline vocabulary, shifting from plain reporting to technical attribution?

observations.why: The 'we' enacts communal-sharing — the team as an undifferentiated body that ships together, not an individual crediting themselves.
Velocity points frame work as proportional output — a market-pricing metric of cost/benefit delivered, not communal effort or rank.
Naming an integration as 'the key unlock' frames a shared enabler of collective progress — communal-sharing's we-ness, the team unlocked together.

payload.focus: Sprint retro: async decision widget shipped, velocity 23 points, Zephyr integration as key unlock
payload.rationale: This sprint retro touches three overlapping regions: (1) the Zephyr integration as key unlock — covered by Position_ZephyrIntegrationUnlock and Obs_ZephyrRateLimitResolved; (2) velocity and metric-anchored claims — covered by Obs_TinaVelocity and StyleObs_Sprint4_MetricAnchor; (3) the async decision widget as proof of the product thesis — covered by Position_Sprint4ThesisProven, Narrative_DecisionCaptureAtConsensus, and Position_CoreFeatureDecisionCapture. I also expanded the Anti-Slack positioning subtree (Narrative_AntiSlackPositioning and its four children) because the widget embodies the anti-Slack thesis and the pricing/category/target-market positions provide context the passes need to place this retro against the broader product vision. No areas were deliberately excluded — the document is short and every concept it names has a direct graph counterpart.

Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage).
